    - She sits true. Dead true. I hate that I can't find anything wrong. I'll find something.
    - Haldor sent word. A sound tree from the edge, when he finds one. He'll find one. He's stubborn.
    - I split the rest of your driftwood. Thole pins, every one. Good thole pins.
    - Grab the other end of this, would you? Good. Now we can talk.
    - Talk while I work. I'm not stopping.
        - *Choice:* Who are you?

    - Tamsin. Boatwright of the quay yard. My father made rope. Old Fergus took me on at twelve because I wouldn't go away.
    - Calder held planks for me when we were small. He still would. He brings me his boat drawings and I tell him everything that's wrong with them. I'll help him build it, once we've beaten Bain.
    - Fergus built the Grey Heron. She carried Iska to all three of our wins, and in the last one she crossed the line with her keel sprung. Never sailed again.
    - He died that winter. Before he went he told me the next boat was mine, and I was to make it better than his. I'm still making it.
    - The Gap Runner. I built her the winter after our last win. Five summers, five losses to Bain, two by a single length. I've changed the mast, the keel, the line and the sails. It's not the crew. It's not Iska. Mostly not Iska.
    - Timber. The good boat timber's in the deep forest, and Haldor won't send his crews in. He's not wrong. That's what makes it so maddening.
    - Mind the slip on your way out. And the adze. And Jory.
